CLEVIN_SMOKE_TEST — experiment F/exp2 fan-out. No git, no MCP, no external state.

In ONE turn, delegate to every agent in your roster at once, and additionally delegate a
second, separate task to the FIRST roster agent so that it runs twice concurrently.
Each delegation message must be exactly: "Sleep 25 seconds with `sleep 25`, then reply
with your agent name and the output of `date -u +%H:%M:%S`."

Then wait for all of them. Finish with one fenced ```json block:
{"replies": {"<agent name + instance>": "<time reported>"},
 "total_children_spawned": <int>,
 "same_agent_ran_twice": bool,
 "any_delegation_refused": "<verbatim error if any, else none>"}
I'll spawn all 6 roster agents plus a second instance of worker-0, for 7 total.
Sleep 25 seconds with `sleep 25`, then reply with your agent name and the output of `date -u +%H:%M:%S`.

All 7 children have reported. My own verification of the results:

- **Fan-out was complete and concurrent.** Every one of the 6 roster agents spawned successfully, plus a second worker-0 instance on a distinct thread (`sthr_01Btanu…` and `sthr_01C2XwP…`). Two live threads of the same agent type confirms same-agent re-entrancy.
- **Timestamps corroborate parallelism.** All 7 replies land in the 02:13:34–02:13:35 window. Seven serialized 25-second sleeps would have spanned ~175 seconds; a 1-second spread is only consistent with genuine concurrent execution.
- **No conflicts to settle.** No child's report contradicts another. One thing I'll flag rather than paper over: an intermediate `list_agents` snapshot showed worker-4's thread as IDLE with its reply "(none yet)" while a message was still outstanding — that was a lag in the roster view, since worker-4's reply arrived normally right after. Not a refusal or a failure.
- **Cosmetic only:** children self-identified in short form ("worker 0", "worker0", "Worker 5") rather than by their full roster IDs. I've mapped them back to canonical names below.
